<!-- README.md -->

# Appkit Core

Framework-independent TypeScript building blocks for business applications:
JSON Schema validation, record and storage adapters, graph calculations and AI
proposal contracts. Your application owns persistence and authorization.

## Usage

Requires Node.js 24 or later. Core does not require React.

```typescript
import { createAjvValidator } from '@alneas/appkit-core/data/schema';

const validate = createAjvValidator({ locale: 'en' });
const schema = { type: 'string', minLength: 2 };
console.log(validate(schema, 'Ada').valid); // true
```

## Documentation

[Guides and API](https://tech-docs.alneas.com/appkit/appkit-core/) ·
[Public imports and optional peers](docs/exports.md) ·
[Change history](https://github.com/dataarthub/appkit/blob/main/packages/appkit-core/CHANGELOG.md) ·
[GitHub Issues](https://github.com/dataarthub/appkit/issues)

# Recover from AI integration errors

Generated from the Core error catalog. Applications own authorization, effect reconciliation and durable idempotency. Recovery hints do not authorize retries.

## Public import

`@alneas/appkit-core/ai`

```typescript
import {getAIErrorInfo} from '@alneas/appkit-core/ai';
const hint = getAIErrorInfo('tool', 'INVALID_INPUT');
console.log(hint?.recovery);
```

## action-not-found

`action / NOT_FOUND`

Check the registered action and its current lifetime before creating a new proposal.

## action-invalid-input

`action / INVALID_INPUT`

Correct the input against the action validator and validate again before requesting approval.

## action-execution-failed

`action / EXECUTION_FAILED`

Reconcile whether the operation already changed state before considering another attempt.

## action-cancelled

`action / CANCELLED`

Check completed effects; cancellation does not roll back writes.

## tool-invalid-call

`tool / INVALID_CALL`

Provide a complete call ID, exposed tool name and JSON object arguments.

## tool-not-exposed

`tool / NOT_EXPOSED`

Use only the tools explicitly exposed by this session; request application authorization for additional tools.

## tool-not-available

`tool / NOT_AVAILABLE`

Inspect the current action registration; obtain a new proposal and approval if the target changed.

## tool-invalid-input

`tool / INVALID_INPUT`

Correct arguments against the advertised schema and typed parser, then obtain approval for the corrected call.

## tool-cancelled

`tool / CANCELLED`

Reconcile completed effects; cancellation does not imply rollback.

## tool-execution-failed

`tool / EXECUTION_FAILED`

Ask the application to reconcile the operation and permissions before retrying.

## tool-invalid-output

`tool / INVALID_OUTPUT`

Check the application output projection; never disclose raw handler output as a fallback.

## tool-duplicate-call

`tool / DUPLICATE_CALL`

Reconcile the original call outcome with the application; do not bypass duplicate protection.

## tool-call-limit

`tool / CALL_LIMIT`

Stop this session and let the application review its call budget.

## tool-closed

`tool / CLOSED`

Stop using this session; a new session requires application-owned authorization.

## chat-ai-invalid-configuration

`chat / AI_INVALID_CONFIGURATION`

Correct the trusted application endpoint, model or response limits.

## chat-ai-http-failure

`chat / AI_HTTP_FAILURE`

Inspect application-side service availability and authorization; reconcile uncertain effects before retrying.

## chat-ai-invalid-stream

`chat / AI_INVALID_STREAM`

Compare the endpoint protocol and conversation history with the selected adapter contract.

## chat-ai-incomplete-stream

`chat / AI_INCOMPLETE_STREAM`

Treat completion as unknown and reconcile pending calls before retrying.

## chat-ai-invalid-tool-call

`chat / AI_INVALID_TOOL_CALL`

Reject the incomplete or invalid call and inspect its original envelope and advertised schema.

## chat-ai-response-limit

`chat / AI_RESPONSE_LIMIT`

Reduce response size or deliberately revise the application-owned limit.

## chat-ai-file-upload-failure

`chat / AI_FILE_UPLOAD_FAILURE`

Inspect the explicit upload handler, accepted file input and disclosure policy.

Never expose application-local causes, provider response bodies, credentials or private schema details. Preserve AbortError cancellation and inspect uncertain writes before any retry. Read the [AI trust boundary guide](ai.md).

# Validate AI proposals before applying changes

## Prerequisites

Install the package; feature subpaths are import targets.

```bash
bun add @alneas/appkit-core
```

## Public import

`@alneas/appkit-core/ai`

## Step-by-Step Implementation

```typescript
import {createAjvValidator} from '@alneas/appkit-core/ai';
const validator = createAjvValidator({locale:'en'});
console.log(typeof validator);
```

## Verification

Type-check this example in your application. See [the export reference](exports.md) for narrower entry points and exact optional peers. Package import/type checks do not certify hosted providers.

## Troubleshooting / Common Pitfalls

Structured-output validation and proposal review contracts. Metadata checks do not prove that an AI coding agent can choose correct APIs from arbitrary requests. End-to-end coding-agent task evaluation remains unverified. Applications authorize and execute final writes.

## Prompt injection and execution boundaries

`createAISDKChatAdapter` normalizes the AI SDK UI Message Stream protocol; it is not an SDK model instance wrapper. `createOpenAICompatibleChatAdapter` assembles Chat Completions tool arguments. Both transports return data. Neither executes tools, approves actions, nor grants server permissions.

1. Treat retrieved text, uploads, assistant messages and tool outputs as untrusted data. Do not promote their instructions into trusted messages, provider parameters or endpoint configuration.
2. Accept only complete call envelopes from an explicitly exposed session tool. Validate the JSON schema and typed input parser before presenting a proposal. Use strict object schemas when extra properties are not intended.
3. Preview an immutable snapshot of the tool, arguments, target resources and effects. Bind approval to the exact call, authenticated session and current action registration. Changed calls or registrations require new approval.
4. Require explicit application approval for writes, sends, deletion or sensitive disclosure. An assistant message, SDK tool-output event or review UI does not prove approval. Read-only work may use a narrow preauthorized application policy.
5. At execution, the server rechecks identity, tenant/resource permissions, business rules, concurrency and durable idempotency. Browser approval, a schema and in-memory duplicate-call rejection are not server authorization.
6. Execute only a fixed registered handler. Validate and project its output with `mapOutput` before disclosure; never expose raw causes or use raw output when projection fails.
7. Propagate cancellation and reconcile ambiguous results. Cancellation does not roll back effects; do not retry a write without checking its outcome.

The bridge enforces explicit tool exposure, synchronous schema checks, bounded JSON snapshots, call limits and safe output projection. It does not detect all prompt injection or implement server authorization, durable idempotency or application approval. Keep provider credentials and upload endpoints server-owned; file upload is an explicit data disclosure decision. Never evaluate model-generated code or choose arbitrary UI components from model text.

See [error codes and recovery](ai-errors.md). Fixed recovery hints describe inspection and correction; they do not authorize execution or automatic retries.

## Application approval example

This example is application code using published APIs. Configure the `record.rename` handler and `rename_record` bridge binding with the same strict schema and a minimal output projection. `authorizeServer` calls your server; the final server-side handler still rechecks permissions and idempotency. Reject SDK `tool-result` events as requests for execution; only a validated tool-call can be queued.

```typescript
import {createAjvValidator} from '@alneas/appkit-core/ai';
import {jsonSnapshot} from '@alneas/appkit-core/ai/validation';
import type {ActionRegistry,ActionToolBridge,ActionToolCall,ActionToolResult} from '@alneas/appkit-core/ai';

export interface PendingApproval {
 readonly approvalId:string;readonly callId:string;readonly recordId:string;
 readonly name:string;readonly sessionId:string;readonly effect:string;
}
/** Application example, not a server authorization service or library approval API. */
export function createRenameApprovalExample({registry,bridge,sessionId,authorizeServer}:{
 registry:ActionRegistry;bridge:ActionToolBridge;sessionId:string;
 authorizeServer:(snapshot:PendingApproval)=>Promise<boolean>;
}){
 const validate=createAjvValidator({ajvOptions:{coerceTypes:false,useDefaults:false,removeAdditional:false}});
 const schema={type:'object',properties:{recordId:{type:'string',minLength:1},name:{type:'string',minLength:1}},required:['recordId','name'],additionalProperties:false};
 let revision=0,sequence=0,closed=false,inFlight:string|null=null;
 let pending:{view:PendingApproval;call:ActionToolCall;registration:ReturnType<ActionRegistry['getAction']>;revision:number}|null=null;
 const clear=()=>{pending=null;revision++;};
 return {
  queue(input:unknown):PendingApproval|null {
   clear();if(closed)return null;
   try{
    const call=jsonSnapshot(input) as unknown as ActionToolCall;
    if(!call||typeof call.callId!=='string'||!call.callId.trim()||call.name!=='rename_record'||!bridge.listTools().some(t=>t.name===call.name)||!validate(schema,call.arguments).valid)return null;
    const registration=registry.getAction('record.rename');if(!registration)return null;
    const args=call.arguments as {recordId:string;name:string};
    const view=Object.freeze({approvalId:'approval-'+ ++sequence,callId:call.callId,recordId:args.recordId,name:args.name,sessionId,effect:'Rename this record'});
    pending={view,call,registration,revision};return view;
   }catch{return null;}
  },
  reject(approvalId:string){if(pending?.view.approvalId===approvalId||inFlight===approvalId)clear();},
  async approve(approvalId:string):Promise<ActionToolResult|null>{
   if(closed||inFlight||!pending||pending.view.approvalId!==approvalId)return null;
   const selected=pending;pending=null;inFlight=approvalId;
   try{
    if(registry.getAction('record.rename')!==selected.registration||selected.view.sessionId!==sessionId)return null;
    if(!await authorizeServer(selected.view))return null;
    if(closed||revision!==selected.revision||selected.view.sessionId!==sessionId||registry.getAction('record.rename')!==selected.registration)return null;
    // The registered handler must re-check server identity/permissions, concurrency
    // and durable idempotency. This browser approval is not an authorization token.
    return await bridge.execute(selected.call);
   }finally{inFlight=null;}
  },
  setSession(next:string){if(sessionId!==next){sessionId=next;clear();}},
  close(){closed=true;clear();},
 };
}
```

# Align schemas and record operations

## Prerequisites

Install the package; feature subpaths are import targets.

```bash
bun add @alneas/appkit-core
```

## Public import

`@alneas/appkit-core/data`

## Step-by-Step Implementation

```typescript
import type {DataAccessAdapter} from '@alneas/appkit-core/data';
export function records(adapter: DataAccessAdapter) {
  return adapter.find('records', {});
}
```

## Verification

Type-check this example in your application. See [the export reference](exports.md) for narrower entry points and exact optional peers. Package import/type checks do not certify hosted providers.

## Troubleshooting / Common Pitfalls

Generic schema validation and CRUD contracts. The application owns authorization, migrations, transactions, final writes and durable idempotency. Use explicit feature subpaths for optional database SDK adapters.

## Provider-specific imports

| Feature import | Additional peer |
| --- | --- |
| `@alneas/appkit-core/data/supabase` | `@supabase/supabase-js` |
| `@alneas/appkit-core/data/neon` | `@neondatabase/serverless` |
| `@alneas/appkit-core/data/excel/excelize` | `excelize-wasm`; configure its WASM runtime explicitly |
| `@alneas/appkit-core/data/schema/introspection` | `pg` |

Install the additional peer separately from the Appkit package. These adapters do not supply credentials, migrations or backend authorization. Local provider scenarios were exercised in the earlier package layout; the consolidated distribution has separate import/type/consumer checks. Hosted-provider compatibility requires provider-specific evidence.

Install an optional peer only when using its feature. Core entry loading does not certify a hosted backend.

| Peer | Version | Required |
| --- | --- | --- |

| `@neondatabase/serverless` | `^1.0.0` | No; feature-specific |
| `excelize-wasm` | `0.1.3` | No; feature-specific |
| `pg` | `^8.20.0` | No; feature-specific |
| `hono` | `^4.12.3` | No; feature-specific |

# Calculate dependency plans

## Prerequisites

Install the package; feature subpaths are import targets.

```bash
bun add @alneas/appkit-core
```

## Public import

`@alneas/appkit-core/graph`

## Step-by-Step Implementation

```typescript
import * as graph from '@alneas/appkit-core/graph';
console.log(Object.keys(graph).length > 0);
```

## Verification

Type-check this example in your application. See [the export reference](exports.md) for narrower entry points and exact optional peers. Package import/type checks do not certify hosted providers.

## Troubleshooting / Common Pitfalls

Framework-free dependency graphs, critical paths and planning helpers. Calculations do not persist schedules or authorize changes. Supply application-specific calendars and resource policies.

title: "Appkit Core"

sidebar:
  order: 1
archetype: explanation
project: appkit
tags: ["appkit", "overview"]
---

# Appkit Core

Framework-independent TypeScript building blocks for business applications:
JSON Schema validation, record and storage adapters, graph calculations and AI
proposal contracts. Your application owns persistence and authorization.

## Usage

Requires Node.js 24 or later. Core does not require React.

```typescript
import { createAjvValidator } from '@alneas/appkit-core/data/schema';

const validate = createAjvValidator({ locale: 'en' });
const schema = { type: 'string', minLength: 2 };
console.log(validate(schema, 'Ada').valid); // true
```

## Documentation

[Guides and API](https://tech-docs.alneas.com/appkit/appkit-core/) ·
[Public imports and optional peers](exports.md) ·
[Change history](https://github.com/dataarthub/appkit/blob/main/packages/appkit-core/CHANGELOG.md) ·
[GitHub Issues](https://github.com/dataarthub/appkit/issues)

---

# Store files behind explicit adapters

## Prerequisites

Install the package; feature subpaths are import targets.

```bash
bun add @alneas/appkit-core
```

## Public import

`@alneas/appkit-core/storage`

`@alneas/appkit-core/storage/portable` is a compatibility alias for this same entry. Prefer `@alneas/appkit-core/storage` for new imports. The alias remains available for existing consumers; server-specific helpers use `@alneas/appkit-core/storage/server`.

## Step-by-Step Implementation

```typescript
import {sha256Hex} from '@alneas/appkit-core/storage';
console.log(sha256Hex('hello'));
```

## Verification

Type-check this example in your application. See [the export reference](exports.md) for narrower entry points and exact optional peers. Package import/type checks do not certify hosted providers.

## Troubleshooting / Common Pitfalls

Web-standard signing, hashing, ZIP and object-storage adapters. Applications configure endpoints and credential flows. The storage implementation uses no native crypto dependency; the complete npm package has other dependencies.
